title: Sarah McBride Becomes The First Trans Member Of Congressional Leadership In A 248-Vote Landslide
text:
Sarah McBride Becomes The First Trans Member Of Congressional Leadership In A 248-Vote Landslide 
 Erin In The Morning 
 Subscribe Sign in 번역 Sarah McBride Becomes The First Trans Member Of Congressional Leadership In A 248-Vote Landslide
 McBride won the role of Democratic Policy and Communications Committee co-chair on Thursday.
 Erin Reed Nov 19, 2026 1,853 32 307 Share Source: McBride.house.gov Erin In The Morning is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a subscriber.
 Subscribe The 2026 elections brought groundbreaking victories for transgender people. Trans people now hold elected office in more states than ever before, and a trans woman even won in a conservative district in Alabama. But transgender people aren’t just winning elections; they’re climbing the ranks of the Democratic Party. Last week in Montana, Rep. Zooey Zephyr was elected minority whip and nonbinary Rep. SJ Howell was elected minority leader. Now a transgender lawmaker has reached an even bigger stage: elected leadership in Congress. On Thursday, Rep. Sarah McBride, D-Del., was elected one of three co-chairs of the House Democratic Policy and Communications Committee , receiving the most votes of any candidate in the race, making her the first transgender person to hold an elected leadership role in Congress. 
 The Democratic Policy and Communications Committee is the messaging arm of the House Democratic Caucus. According to multiple sources in the room cited by Axios’ Andrew Solender, McBride received 248 votes, the most of the four candidates running for three co-chair seats. Rep. Maxwell Frost, D-FL, received 195 votes and Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove, D-CA, received 180 votes. The three will serve as co-chairs of the committee in the next Congress.
 The committee’s role is to develop messaging for House Democrats and to contrast their policy priorities with Republican policies. When McBride announced her bid for co-chair in September, she wrote to colleagues that she wanted the caucus to “hit the ground running with a unified message” and manage an “increasingly complex media environment,” according to a copy of the letter reviewed by EITM. She specifically proposed engaging more with new media influencers and podcasters, who have taken an outsized role in recent political debates.
 The role has launched leadership careers for several other Democrats in the past. In 2016, Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, whom the caucus nominated for speaker on Wednesday, was elected a co-chair , the same role McBride will now hold. Rep. Ted Lieu was elected a co-chair in 2018 and was elected caucus chair this week. And Rep. Lauren Underwood was elected to the same role in 2024 and just won the race for House Democratic Caucus vice chair . 
 The vote comes two years after Republicans banned McBride and all transgender people from bathrooms matching their gender in congressional buildings. On Nov. 18, 2024, Rep. Nancy Mace introduced a resolution to ban transgender women from women’s restrooms, and Speaker Mike Johnson adopted the policy two days later. McBride’s reaction to that debacle came under some criticism from within the transgender community for her unwillingness to violate the ban. Still, two years later, Mace is not returning to Congress , and McBride will take a leadership role in a Congress that is likely to restore her ability to use the bathroom in peace. 
 McBride’s colleagues were quick to celebrate her election. Majority Democrats, a group of elected Democratic lawmakers, posted, “Congrats to Majority Dem Rep. Sarah McBride on being elected co-chair of the House Democratic Policy and Communications Committee! She's a rising Democratic star, and we’re glad she’ll be helping shape our party’s messaging so everyone across America hears it loud and clear.” Now, in the largest Democratic congress in a generation, a transgender person will help shape the messaging for the party moving forward.
